function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content: Electricity isn’t the discovery of a single person—it’s a natural phenomenon that has been known since antiquity. The first recorded observations were made by Thales of Miletus around 600 BC, who noticed that rubbing amber produced a static charge. Over the next few centuries, scholars such as William Gilbert (who coined the term “electricus” in the early 1600s), Benjamin Franklin (mid‑1700s, famous for his kite experiment), Alessandro Volta (invented the voltaic pile in 1800), and Michael Faraday (discovered electromagnetic induction in the 1830s) laid the foundations of modern electrical science. Thus, the “discovery” of electricity is really a cumulative effort spanning many generations.
